column1: # Taskr #209 - the EXTRACTION endpoint round trip measured from a phone, 2026-09-08.
# Device      Samsung SM-S918U, Android 16, curl 8.15.0-DEV in `adb shell` over USB.
#             No browser, so nothing here is attributable to one or to a service worker.
# Function    extract-description, deployment v2, ezbr_sha256
#             deployed 2026-09-08T01:47:25.642Z by this story.
# Analysis    docs/hosting-decision.md, section "Measured 2026-09-08".
# #205 measured the same path with `provision-member`, which refuses at its first
# authorization check - so it timed everything EXCEPT the endpoint own work and the
# provider call. This measures the whole thing, keeping #205 method so the two are
# comparable. Each cycle fires three calls seconds apart on one network:
#   level 1  no Authorization header       the GATEWAY refuses. Nothing boots.
#   level 2  publishable key only          the function boots and refuses.
#   level 3  real session + own household   the full extraction, provider included.
# So 3 minus 2 is the endpoint own work plus the provider, as a per-sample
# subtraction rather than an estimate, and 2 minus 1 is the boot. Levels are
# classified from the body that came back, never from which call was meant to be
# sent: 0 of 252 came back mislabelled.
# Networks    wifi  = first pass, on a DEGRADED link - read its level 1 control before
#                     reading anything else in it (p95 3698 ms against the other passes
#                     571 and 1403). Kept rather than discarded: it is a real evening.
#             cellular = wifi switched off for the pass and switched back on after, because
#                     `curl --interface rmnet_dataN` binds but has no route from the adb
#                     shell UID on this build ("Network is unreachable"), so #205 method of
#                     reaching both networks without touching device state did not reproduce.
#             wifi2 = second wifi pass, after the link settled.
#             The public egress address differed between the wifi and cellular passes
#             (sha256 a39562036a08 against 850410d5a84e), which is the control that the two
#             really are two networks. The addresses themselves are this household broadband
#             and cellular IPs and this repo is public, so no address column exists at all -
#             #205 carried one and redacted it; this one was never collected.
# Each pass ran against its OWN fixture household, created through the seeded test
# account and deleted afterwards with the absence read back. 84 level-3 calls in all,
# 28 per household, inside the 60-per-household-per-hour bound in handler.ts RATE_LIMIT.
# Times are seconds as curl reports them. The body column is truncated at 140 bytes.
# There are exactly three distinct bodies across all 252 rows.
